title: Posterior Regularization for Structured Latent Variable Models
authors: Kuzman Ganchev, João Graça, Jennifer Gillenwater, Ben Taskar
conclusions: Introduces posterior regularization (PR), a framework that incorporates indirect/weak supervision into structured latent-variable models via linear constraints on the EXPECTATIONS of posterior distributions over unlabeled data, rather than on model parameters.

Constraints are defined corpus-wide as Q = {q(Y): E_q[phi(X,Y)] <= b} (optionally with slack), and training maximizes a KL-regularized likelihood J_Q(theta) = L(theta) - KL(Q || p_theta(Y|X)) via a modified EM/coordinate-ascent scheme with an efficient dual (projected gradient/L-BFGS).

Framework applies to both generative and discriminative models and unifies/relates to constraint-driven learning (Chang et al.), generalized expectation criteria (Mann & McCallum), and Bayesian measurements (Liang et al.).

Demonstrated on four NLP applications: statistical word alignment (bijectivity + symmetry constraints), multi-view learning, cross-lingual dependency grammar induction, and unsupervised POS induction (sparsity constraints), each showing constraints substantially improve over unconstrained EM.

Constraints hold only in expectation over the (unlabeled) posterior, not as hard per-instance guarantees; enforcing genuinely hard constraints would in general break tractable structure (e.g., factorization) of the underlying model.
On unseen/held-out unlabeled data, learned parameters may only approximately satisfy the constraints, even though they were enforced during training on the observed unlabeled corpus.

Our constraint is transductive in exactly this sense, ... but it is hard: an explicit argmax count budget ... with per-group caps, enforced during training of a deep classifier.' The citation supports the specific, narrow claim that PR constrains posterior expectations over unlabeled data; our paper contrasts this against its own hard argmax-count constraint.
